title: Coordinate Geometry
description: Master the 2D Cartesian plane, coordinate pairs, quadrants, linear graphs, and gridline distances through interactive visual discovery.
subject: Mathematics

learnBlocks.content: A coordinate plane lets us describe any position with two numbers: how far right (or left) we go, then how far up (or down) we go. The two lines that divide the plane are the x-axis (horizontal) and the y-axis (vertical). They meet at the origin, point (0, 0).

steps.title: 1. Move Right (x-axis)
steps.instruction: Move the point 3 grid steps to the right along the x-axis.
steps.explanation: The horizontal line is the x-axis. Moving right increases the x-coordinate from 0 to 3.

steps.title: 2. Move Up (y-axis)
steps.instruction: Now move the point 2 grid steps up along the y-axis.
steps.explanation: The vertical line is the y-axis. Moving up increases the y-coordinate from 0 to 2.

steps.title: 3. Both Directions
steps.instruction: Move the point 3 steps right and 2 steps up to reach (3, 2).
steps.explanation: Combine the axes: 3 steps right sets x = 3, then 2 steps up sets y = 2. The pair is (3, 2).

evaluateBlocks.question: What are the coordinates of the origin on a 2D Cartesian plane?
evaluateBlocks.explanation: The origin is point (0, 0) where the x-axis and y-axis intersect.

evaluateBlocks.question: Which axis is horizontal?
evaluateBlocks.explanation: The x-axis runs horizontally (left to right); the y-axis runs vertically.

learnBlocks.content: On the x-axis you can only move right or left. Moving right increases your x-coordinate while the y-coordinate stays 0.

steps.title: 1. Walk 4 Right
steps.instruction: Move the point 4 grid steps to the right.
steps.explanation: 4 steps right takes x from 0 to 4. The y-coordinate stays 0.

steps.title: 2. Walk 5 Right
steps.instruction: Move the point 5 more grid steps to the right.
steps.explanation: 5 steps right takes x from 0 to 5, so you land at (5, 0).

steps.title: 3. Spot (4, 0)
steps.instruction: Select the point that is 4 steps right of the origin.
steps.explanation: 4 steps right with no up or down lands on (4, 0).

evaluateBlocks.question: Starting at the origin, you move 4 steps right. Where are you?
evaluateBlocks.explanation: Moving right only changes the x-coordinate, so you reach (4, 0).

evaluateBlocks.question: What is the y-coordinate of every point on the x-axis?
evaluateBlocks.explanation: Every point on the x-axis has a y-coordinate of 0.

learnBlocks.content: On the y-axis you can only move up or down. Moving up increases your y-coordinate while the x-coordinate stays 0.

steps.title: 1. Climb 3
steps.instruction: Move the point 3 grid steps up.
steps.explanation: 3 steps up takes y from 0 to 3. The x-coordinate stays 0.

steps.title: 2. Climb 5
steps.instruction: Move the point 5 grid steps up.
steps.explanation: 5 steps up takes y from 0 to 5, so you land at (0, 5).

steps.title: 3. Spot (0, 2)
steps.instruction: Select the point that is 2 steps up from the origin.
steps.explanation: 2 steps up with no right or left lands on (0, 2).

evaluateBlocks.question: Starting at the origin, you move 3 steps up. Where are you?
evaluateBlocks.explanation: Moving up only changes the y-coordinate, so you reach (0, 3).

evaluateBlocks.question: What is the x-coordinate of every point on the y-axis?
evaluateBlocks.explanation: Every point on the y-axis has an x-coordinate of 0.

learnBlocks.content: Coordinates always come as a pair (x, y). The first number x tells you how far to move right, and the second number y tells you how far to move up. A point is the combination of both moves.

steps.title: 1. Reach (3, 2)
steps.instruction: Move the point 3 steps right and 2 steps up to reach (3, 2).
steps.explanation: 3 steps right sets x = 3, then 2 steps up sets y = 2: the point (3, 2).

steps.title: 2. Reach (4, 5)
steps.instruction: Move the point 4 steps right and 5 steps up to reach (4, 5).
steps.explanation: 4 steps right sets x = 4, then 5 steps up sets y = 5: the point (4, 5).

steps.title: 3. Reach (5, 1)
steps.instruction: Move the point 5 steps right and 1 step up to reach (5, 1).
steps.explanation: 5 steps right sets x = 5, then 1 step up sets y = 1: the point (5, 1).

evaluateBlocks.question: If you move 4 steps right and 2 steps up from the origin, what is your coordinate pair?
evaluateBlocks.explanation: Coordinates are written as (x, y). 4 steps right = 4, 2 steps up = 2, so the pair is (4, 2).

evaluateBlocks.question: In the coordinate pair (5, 3), what does the number 5 represent?
options: The distance from the origin along the diagonal
evaluateBlocks.explanation: The first number 5 is the x-coordinate, which measures the horizontal position.

learnBlocks.content: To plot a point, first go right along the x-axis, then go up along the y-axis. Every coordinate pair (x, y) points to exactly one location on the plane.

steps.title: 1. Plot (3, 1)
steps.instruction: Select the point that is 3 steps right and 1 step up from the origin.
steps.explanation: 3 right gives x = 3, 1 up gives y = 1, so the pair is (3, 1).

steps.title: 2. Plot (4, 3)
steps.instruction: Select the point at (4, 3).
steps.explanation: The first number is the x-coordinate (horizontal), the second is the y-coordinate (vertical): (4, 3).

steps.title: 3. Plot (5, 2)
steps.instruction: Select the point at (5, 2).
steps.explanation: 5 right and 2 up gives the point (5, 2).

evaluateBlocks.question: Which point is at (4, 3)?
evaluateBlocks.explanation: The pair (4, 3) means 4 steps right first, then 3 steps up.

learnBlocks.content: The order in a coordinate pair matters! (5, 2) is NOT the same as (2, 5). The first number is always the horizontal move; the second is always the vertical move.

steps.title: 1. Find (5, 2)
steps.instruction: Select the point at (5, 2).
steps.explanation: (5, 2) means 5 right first, then 2 up — far from the y-axis.

steps.title: 2. Find (2, 5)
steps.instruction: Select the point at (2, 5).
steps.explanation: (2, 5) means only 2 right, but 5 up — tall and close to the y-axis.

steps.title: 3. Find (1, 4)
steps.instruction: Select the point at (1, 4).
steps.explanation: (1, 4) is 1 right and 4 up; (4, 1) would be 4 right and 1 up.

evaluateBlocks.question: Which point is further to the right: (5, 2) or (2, 5)?
evaluateBlocks.explanation: The first number is the horizontal move, so (5, 2) with x = 5 is further right than (2, 5).

evaluateBlocks.question: What does the second number in a coordinate pair tell you?
options: The total distance from the origin
evaluateBlocks.explanation: The second number y is the vertical position: how far up you move.

learnBlocks.content: When two points lie on the same horizontal gridline (same y), the distance between them is simply the difference of their x-coordinates: |x2 - x1|. Count the grid steps to check.

steps.title: 1. Distance of 5
steps.instruction: Observe the horizontal distance from the origin to point (5, 0).
steps.explanation: The horizontal distance is |5 - 0| = 5 grid steps.

steps.title: 2. Distance of 4
steps.instruction: Observe the vertical distance from the origin to point (0, 4).
steps.explanation: The vertical distance is |4 - 0| = 4 grid steps.

steps.title: 3. Count to (4, 3)
steps.instruction: Observe the horizontal (4) and vertical (3) distances that reach (4, 3).
steps.explanation: From the origin, 4 steps right then 3 steps up reaches (4, 3).

evaluateBlocks.question: What is the horizontal distance between point A(2, 3) and point B(7, 3)?
evaluateBlocks.explanation: Both points share y = 3, so distance = |7 - 2| = 5 units.

evaluateBlocks.question: What is the vertical distance between point A(4, 1) and point B(4, 6)?
evaluateBlocks.explanation: Both points share x = 4, so distance = |6 - 1| = 5 units.

learnBlocks.content: Moving left along the x-axis or down along the y-axis gives negative values.

evaluateBlocks.question: Which direction do you move for a negative x-coordinate?
evaluateBlocks.explanation: Negative x-values lie to the left of the y-axis.

learnBlocks.content: A horizontal line has equation y = c. A vertical line has equation x = k.

evaluateBlocks.question: What is the equation of a horizontal line passing through y = 4?
evaluateBlocks.explanation: Every point on a horizontal line has constant y-value.

learnBlocks.content: An inequality divides the Cartesian plane into half-planes above/below or left/right of boundary lines.

evaluateBlocks.question: Which half-plane represents y > 2?
options: The region strictly above the line y = 2
evaluateBlocks.correctAnswer: The region strictly above the line y = 2
evaluateBlocks.explanation: y > 2 includes all points with y-coordinate greater than 2.

learnBlocks.content: For points on the same horizontal line (y1 = y2), distance = |x2 - x1|.

evaluateBlocks.question: What is the horizontal distance between point A(2, 3) and point B(7, 3)?
